ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Liliʻuokalani

code.originalText: Five-week review: rhythm monitor result, anticoagulation decision, lipids, kidney function and blood pressure

text.paragraph: Five-week review: rhythm monitor result and anticoagulation. [S]

Liliʻuokalani returns five weeks after the stroke, with a member of her ʻohana. The 30-day monitor recorded six episodes of atrial fibrillation, the longest 3 hours 10 minutes, about 3% of the time, none of which she felt. She finished 21 days of aspirin and clopidogrel two weeks ago and now takes clopidogrel alone, with no bleeding. Her home blood pressure averaged 138/82 in the week after the stroke, so losartan 25 mg was started a week after the event; her home average is now 126/76. The potassium and creatinine check two weeks after starting losartan did not happen: the member of her household who drives her was away, and she did not want to trouble anyone. She has had no new neurological symptoms and plays the piano every morning. She has begun lomilomi with a practitioner at Ke Ola Mamo, who was told about her blood thinners. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-20; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 130/78, pulse 74 and regular; weight 57.8 kg
Speech fluent; no drift; normal fine finger movements; normal gait

Transient weakness and clumsiness of the right hand with word-finding difficulty, lasting about 20 minutes and fully resolved, the afternoon before the visit; suspected transient ischemic attack, ABCD2 score 5 (high risk); NIH Stroke Scale 0
S — Synthetic presenting problem; resolved into the stroke diagnosis when diffusion MRI showed a small infarct at the stroke clinic the next day. Not a claim about her real symptoms.

Minor ischemic stroke: a small acute infarct in the cortex of the left precentral gyrus (left middle cerebral artery territory) on diffusion MRI, embolic in pattern, with full recovery (NIH Stroke Scale 0); source found to be paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; synthetic modern episode linked to her documented death from a stroke
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the stroke clinic the day after the visit; the 1917 cause of death remains D.
Hypertension: told of borderline readings in past years and not treated; 156/88 mmHg at intake
S — Synthetic risk factor; no blood pressure from her lifetime is recorded in the cited sources.

list.item:
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, the likely source of the stroke (I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc 6 (age 75 or older, stroke, hypertension, female sex); HAS-BLED 2. An anticoagulant prevents far more strokes than antiplatelets in atrial fibrillation, and the bleeding risk is acceptable. The infarct was small and five weeks old, so it is safe to start now. Full-dose apixaban: she meets only one of the three dose-reduction criteria (age 80 or older, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or more). Creatinine clearance about 49 mL/min. [S]
Stop clopidogrel today.
Start apixaban 5 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart, without missing doses.
Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen and naproxen; acetaminophen for pain.
Blood count and kidney function about every five months.
Tell any practitioner who gives lomilomi or other bodywork that she takes apixaban, and ask for gentle pressure.

Minor ischemic stroke (I63.412). Cardioembolic from atrial fibrillation, with a small carotid plaque. LDL 64 mg/dL on atorvastatin 40 mg, below the goal of 70. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 40 mg; lipid panel in three to four months.

Hypertension (I10). Home average 126/76 and clinic 130/78 on losartan 25 mg; potassium 4.5 mmol/L and creatinine 0.86 mg/dL today. [S]
Continue losartan 25 mg.
Laboratory tests at clinic visits, or at home by the clinic's nurse, so that no separate trip is needed.

text.paragraph: Protocol monitoring: items the monitoring protocol calls for at this visit. [S]

tr.td: Blood pressure in the clinic and at home (target below 130/80 mmHg) and weight
Potassium and creatinine after starting an angiotensin receptor blocker
About two weeks after starting, then every six months

The check due two weeks after losartan was started was missed: the member of her household who drives her was away, and she did not ask anyone else. Today, four weeks after the start, potassium is 4.5 mmol/L and creatinine 0.86 mg/dL (eGFR 69), both normal, so no harm resulted. Corrective action: tests drawn at clinic visits, or at home by the clinic's nurse

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack: A Guideline From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (2021); 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway on Practical Approaches for Arrhythmia Monitoring After Stroke (2024); 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation (2023); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, stroke and transient ischemic attack, atrial fibrillation and hypertension monographs (2026); Signs and Symptoms of Stroke (2026); Ke Ola Mamo: a Native Hawaiian Health Care System serving Oʻahu (medical care, lomilomi and community health workers) (2026)

Follow-up: Three-month review in eight weeks. Call for bleeding that will not stop, black stools or any fall with a blow to the head; call 911 for any BE FAST sign. Next scheduled visit 2026-06-15: three-month review after the stroke: function, mood, blood pressure, apixaban safety and falls. [S]
